This points to a stalk rot disease. Key candidates: Physoderma_Stalk_Rot, Bacterial_Stalk_Rot, Diplodia_Stalk_Rot, Charcoal_Stalk_Rot.

- **Test image**: Green corn stalk with concentrated dark brown/black necrotic lesions at the node junction. Outer sheath partially pulled back reveals darkened node tissue. Stalk is still green/alive.

- **References compared**:
  - Physoderma_Stalk_Rot (17): Dark scattered spots on green stalk sheath — closest match in color and stalk condition
  - Physoderma_Stalk_Rot (56): Severe cross-section rot, darker but internal
  - Bacterial_Stalk_Rot (16): Generalized mushy brown rot, no clear node focus
  - Diplodia_Stalk_Rot (14): Dry tan rot on dead stalk, very different
  - Charcoal_Stalk_Rot (12): Internal shredded dark tissue, very different
  - Anthracnose (10): Dark lesions on dried stalks — stalk is dead, not green like test
  - Physoderma_Brown_Spot (47): Leaf spots with dark midrib lesions — leaf disease

The test image most closely matches Physoderma_Stalk_Rot — dark/black lesions specifically at the node on an otherwise green stalk is the hallmark of Physoderma node rot. No other candidate showed this specific combination of green stalk + concentrated node darkening.
